expected_evidence: geological: a continent-wide 'black mat' or dark organic-rich layer at ~10,950 BCE containing anomalous concentrations of nanodiamonds, magnetic spherules, platinum-group elements (esp. platinum/iridium), charcoal spikes indicating continental-scale biomass burning

astronomical: orbital/dynamical modeling showing Earth crossing a dense filament of the Taurid meteor stream complex (parent body fragmentation debris) around the proposed date, plus any historical/telescopic records of unusually intense Taurid-associated fireball activity (largely inferential, not directly observed at this time depth)
material (archaeological): abrupt disappearance or thinning of Clovis-culture artifact layers directly above/at the purported impact layer across multiple North American sites
genetic: megafaunal (mammoth, mastodon, horse, etc.) ancient DNA showing a sharp population bottleneck or extinction signature dated to ~12,900 cal BP

oral_tradition: Indigenous North American narratives of a catastrophic sky-fire, darkness, or flood event that could be retrospectively linked to the proposed impact (highly speculative and difficult to date/verify)

model-prior: existing published scientific literature on the Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis (Firestone et al. 2007 and successors) versus critical rebuttals (e.g., failure to replicate nanodiamond/platinum signals at some sites, alternative explanations for the black mat and megafaunal decline such as human overhunting or climate-driven vegetation change)
response.rationale: The proposed date (~10,950 BCE) coincides almost exactly with the Younger Dryas onset boundary, so I am treating this as falling in the 'younger-dryas' period row rather than a generic upper-paleolithic one, since that is the period most directly relevant to the mechanism claimed (Taurid-stream/impact-related climatic and extinction event). Geological (0.65) and astronomical (0.7) evidence categories have comparatively high detectability for this period because sedimentary boundary layers and cosmic dust/impact markers can persist for millennia and are actively sampled in modern stratigraphic and geochemical surveys — this matches the real, though contested, scientific literature on the Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis (model-prior, unverified against the actual evidence text provided). Material/archaeological (0.35) and genetic (0.3) evidence are moderately detectable but confounded by preservation gaps and the difficulty of attributing megafaunal decline specifically to an impact versus co-occurring climatic/anthropogenic causes. Oral tradition (0.1) and linguistic (0.05) evidence are essentially undetectable at this time depth — no continuous, verifiable transmission chain of ~13,000-year-old narratives is plausible, so their absence should not be read as evidence against the hypothesis. The 'inconclusive' action in the hypothesis itself is consistent with this evidentiary profile: physical/astronomical proxies are detectable in principle and have in fact been reported at various sites, but replication failures and alternative explanations (per model-prior recollection of the ongoing Firestone-vs-critics debate) mean the surviving evidence is real but interpretively contested rather than absent. A moderate overall detectability adjustment (0.55) reflects that some evidence types are quite recoverable (geological, astronomical) while others (oral, linguistic, textual) are near-zero, and the mixed/contested empirical record should be weighed as partial support tempered by low confidence, not as a low-detectability excuse for total silence.
